Three primary-source pages to check this module's reasoning yourself, plus a regulator video and
six further sources added to go deeper. The first three were curl-verified
(`curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -L <url>`) and returned `200` at the time this page was
written; the later entries each note their own verification.

- **[45 CFR 164.506, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.506)**
  — the treatment/payment/health care operations permission this module leans on hardest. Read
  paragraph (c), which this module's excerpt didn't quote, if you want the full list of what
  counts as a TPO disclosure beyond the standard in (a).

- **[45 CFR 164.512, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.512)**
  — the full public-health-activities section that paragraph (b)(1)(iii) (the FDA-regulated-product
  exception quoted in full above) sits inside. Useful if you ever need one of 164.512's other
  paragraphs (judicial/law-enforcement disclosures, decedents, research) — none of which this
  module quotes or relies on.

- **[45 CFR 164.514, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.514)**
  — the full minimum-necessary section, including paragraphs (a)-(c) and (e)-(g) this module's
  excerpt deliberately left out (de-identification methodology, limited data sets, and
  research/marketing-adjacent provisions). Read (d)(4) and (d)(5) here if you want the rest of the
  minimum-necessary implementation specifications beyond (d)(1)-(3).

- **[Treatment, Payment, & Health Care Operations](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ulV3x_v10Uc)**
  (USGovHHSOCR, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson, from HHS OCR's
  own channel. General HIPAA training on the 164.506 permission, not blood-specific. Verified
  embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.501, definitions](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.501)**
  — the section holding the numbered definition of "health care operations" that this lesson
  flags as not independently fetched. Read it to close that gap yourself before treating the
  deferral-coding review as confirmed. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[45 CFR 164.501, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.501)**
  — the same definitions section on the official eCFR, for the current text. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.502](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.502)** — the full
  general-rules section behind the 164.502(a) default-deny standard, including paragraph (b)
  (minimum necessary) that 164.514(d) implements. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.524](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.524)** — the full
  right-of-access section, including the exceptions and denial provisions this lesson's light
  treatment of (a)(1) and (b)(2) leaves out. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[CMS MLN Fact Sheet: HIPAA Basics for Providers](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/mln909001-hipaa-basics-providers-privacy-security-breach-notification-rules.pdf)**
  — a short federal agency (CMS) fact sheet covering the Privacy, Security, and Breach
  Notification Rules from a provider's point of view; a plain-language orientation to this whole
  course. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Federal Register: HIPAA Privacy Rule To Support Reproductive Health Care Privacy](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/04/26/2024-08503/hipaa-privacy-rule-to-support-reproductive-health-care-privacy)**
  — an official rulemaking document showing how HHS amends 164.502 and related Privacy Rule
  provisions, useful as a sample of how the rule's text actually changes over time; a reason to
  check current eCFR text rather than a dated snapshot. Not about blood establishments. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about the HIPAA Privacy Rule and minimum necessary.

- **[HIPAA Privacy Rule](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-privacy-rule/)** (HIPAA Journal) — an accessible overview of what the rule covers, permitted uses, and individual rights; a good companion to the CFR text in this lesson. Page title: "HIPAA Privacy Rule - Updated for 2026". Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[HIPAA Business Associate Agreement](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-business-associate-agreement/)** (HIPAA Journal) — explains how privacy obligations extend to vendors, which matters whenever an extract leaves the building. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Privacy and Security (ONC)](https://www.healthit.gov/topic/privacy-security-and-hipaa)** (Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT) — a government hub of plain-language guides and fact sheets aimed at people who run health IT, not lawyers. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CISSP: Certified Information Systems Security Professional](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/cissp)** (ISC2) — the official certification page and exam outline. Privacy, data handling and legal/regulatory obligations sit in CISSP Domain 1 (Security and Risk Management) and Domain 2 (Asset Security). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
